feedback.hint: Keep the independently known voltage references distinct from loaded transient reports.
feedback.solution: Each of twelve groups has three deliberately balanced reports. Raw means retain additive offset and gain.

questions.prompt: Independent zero reference has true node voltage 0 V. What reporting offset in V follows from its raw CSV mean? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: Use the independently specified zero-voltage reference.
feedback.solution: The zero reference mean is 0.020 V, identifying the additive reporting offset under the declared affine model.

questions.prompt: Independent cal reference has true node voltage 2.50 V and raw mean 5.020 V; the zero reference raw mean is 0.020 V. What dimensionless reporting gain follows? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: Subtract baseline before dividing by the known reference voltage.
feedback.solution: Gain is (5.020−0.020)/2.50=2. This corrects reporting, without removing physical input loading.

questions.prompt: After reporting calibration, condition A steady node voltage is 10/11 V for a known open-circuit 1.0 V source and known input resistance 1.0 MΩ. What source resistance in Ω follows from the DC divider? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: Solve V_node=V_s R_in/(R_s+R_in) for R_s.
feedback.solution: R_s=1000000×(1/(10/11)−1)=100000 Ω under the stated DC input model.

questions.prompt: Condition B has R_in=100 kΩ,R_s=100 kΩ,initial voltage zero,calibrated V(0.050 s)=0.316060 V and steady voltage 0.50 V. Infer τ from the normalized transition, then C=τ/(R_s parallel R_in). What C in µF follows? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: Normalize by the final voltage, use the remaining fraction logarithm, and identify the resistance seen by the capacitor.
feedback.solution: The remaining fraction is approximately exp(−1), giving τ≈0.050 s. Effective resistance is 50000 Ω, so C=1.0 µF.

questions.prompt: Select conclusions supported by the supplied references and circuit model.

response_fields.prompt: What does subtracting offset and dividing by gain recover?
options: The loaded node voltage, with physical loading still present.
The open-circuit source automatically, regardless of impedance.
A unique biological signal source.

response_fields.prompt: Why do A and B have different observed τ in this construction?
options: Their known input resistance changes the resistance seen by the same input capacitance.
The source generator necessarily changes its intrinsic time scale.
Reporting gain alone changes the ideal circuit differential equation.

response_fields.prompt: What would this dummy-source result establish for the preserved recording case?
options: A conditional electrical loading explanation to compare with independently checked source and input properties.
Proof that every real electrode signal change is purely electrical.
A validated patient measurement method.

evidence: An affine reporting correction is distinct from circuit transfer correction.
The construction changes one input resistance while retaining source and capacitance.
Synthetic circuit predictions do not identify a unique real biological cause.

feedback.hint: Separate independent reference information, physical node response and real-source inference.
feedback.solution: Calibration recovers loaded voltage; changed effective resistance explains changed τ in the construction; real-source interpretation still needs independent evidence.

questions.prompt: Which statements respect the supplied synthetic reports? Select all that apply.
options: A finite input capacitance can change the observed transient even when the source step is unchanged.
Two fitted exponentials uniquely identify every real electrode mechanism.
The three report variants deliberately balance around each rounded group mean.
The three variants prove independent Gaussian instrument noise.
Correcting reporting gain does not by itself undo DC divider attenuation.

feedback.hint: Distinguish constructed repeats, circuit response and the reporting map.
feedback.solution: Balanced variants, finite-input filtering and remaining divider attenuation follow from the construction. Independent noise and unique real mechanisms are not demonstrated.

questions.prompt: For the supplied unchanged source and input capacitance, which A/B prediction is consistent?
options: A has larger steady node voltage and longer τ than B because its input resistance is larger.
B has larger steady voltage because its input resistance is smaller.
A and B have identical steady voltage because reporting is calibrated.

feedback.hint: Use both the DC divider and the parallel resistance seen by the capacitor.
feedback.solution: A steady voltage is 10/11 V and τ=0.090909 s; B gives 0.50 V and τ=0.050 s. Source generator and capacitance remain unchanged.
